<header class="dg-head dg-head-chapter"><p class="dg-kicker">Chapter 2</p><h1 class="dg-title">Vector Spaces</h1></header>
<div class="dg-motivation"><div class="dg-motivation-title">Motivation: Objects that do not depend on a basis</div><div class="dg-motivation-upper"><p>Physical laws should not depend on the basis used to describe them. In <span class="math inline">\(\mathbb{R}^3\)</span>, a vector <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}\)</span> has components that change with the basis,  <span class="math display">\[
        \mathcal{X} = \sum_{i=1}^{3} x^i \, \hat{x}_i = \sum_{i=1}^{3} y^i \, \hat{y}_i ,
        \qquad x^i \neq y^i \text{ in general},
    \]</span>  while <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}\)</span> itself does not. A law written in components therefore holds in every basis precisely when it is the component form of a relation between basis-independent objects. These objects will not always be arrows. The tangent vectors of Chapter <a class="dg-xref" href="../tangent-spaces/index.html" data-kind="chapter" data-label="chapter_Tangent_Spaces">4</a> are directional derivatives acting on functions, yet they are added and rescaled following the same rules. The theory is thus built from these rules alone.</p>
</div><div class="dg-motivation-lower">
<p><strong>Goal.</strong> Develop the algebra that every later chapter applies point by point on a manifold.</p>
<ul class="dg-itemize dg-depth-1">
<li><p>Build, from sets and maps through groups, rings and fields, the axioms of an <strong><span class="math inline">\(\mathbb{R}\)</span>-vector space</strong> and of linear maps.</p></li>
<li><p>Define the <strong>dual space</strong> and <strong>tensors</strong> as multilinear maps, without reference to any basis.</p></li>
<li><p>Introduce bases and derive how components transform under a change of basis, which distinguishes covariant from contravariant objects.</p></li>
</ul>
<p>At every point of a manifold, these constructions become the tangent, cotangent and tensor spaces of Chapter <a class="dg-xref" href="../tangent-spaces/index.html" data-kind="chapter" data-label="chapter_Tangent_Spaces">4</a>.</p></div></div>
<p>Figure <a class="dg-xref" href="../introduction/roadmaps.html#fig_vector_spaces_roadmap" data-kind="figure" data-label="fig_vector_spaces_roadmap">1.2</a> summarizes the hierarchy of structures together with their notation, operations and component transformation laws, and Appendix <a class="dg-xref" href="../examples/example-vector-space.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_Example_vector_space">C.1</a> works out an explicit example with polynomials.</p>
